Full API spec:
Public API and contracts:
- Module: snake_game.direction
  - class Direction(Enum): members UP=(0,-1), DOWN=(0,1), LEFT=(-1,0), RIGHT=(1,0).
    - delta(self) -> tuple[int, int]: returns (dx, dy) exactly as bound to the member; no external duplication of deltas allowed.
    - is_opposite(self, other: Direction) -> bool: returns True iff other is the immediate opposite of self; prevents reversal during Snake.turn.

- Module: snake_game.grid
  - @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Position: fields x:int, y:int; immutable and hashable.
  - class Grid:
    - __init__(self, width: int, height: int): validates width > 0 and height > 0; raises ValueError on invalid.
    - width(self) -> int: returns configured width.
    - height(self) -> int: returns configured height.
    - in_bounds(self, pos: Position) -> bool: returns True iff 0 <= pos.x < width and 0 <= pos.y < height.
  Import rules: grid.py must not import Direction or any movement deltas.

- Module: snake_game.snake
  - class Snake:
    - __init__(self, start: Position, direction: Direction): initializes body with [start] and current direction.
    - turn(self, requested: Direction) -> bool: if requested is opposite of current direction, reject and return False; otherwise set direction and return True.
    - head(self) -> Position: returns current head Position (front of body).
    - next_head(self) -> Position: computes head advanced by current direction.delta().
    - advance(self, grow: bool) -> None: mutates body in place; inserts next_head at front; if grow is False, pops tail; if True, retains tail (growing by 1).
    - body(self) -> list[Position]: returns live reference to internal body list (tests and Game read only).
  Import rules: imports Direction and Position directly; no duplicate delta logic.

- Module: snake_game.collision
  - hit_wall(grid: Grid, pos: Position) -> bool: returns True if pos is out of bounds; otherwise False.
  - hit_self(body: list[Position], next_head: Position, grow: bool) -> bool: returns True if moving into next_head collides with the body; when grow is False, moving into the current tail is safe (tail will depart in the same tick).
  Import rules: does not import Direction; uses only arguments provided.

- Module: snake_game.random_provider
  - class RandomProvider:
    - __init__(self, sequence: Optional[list[Position]] = None, seed: Optional[int] = None): if sequence provided, use as deterministic queue; else initialize with a simple deterministic LCG seeded by 'seed' or a default.
    - next_position(self, grid: Grid) -> Position: returns the next candidate Position within grid bounds. If a sequence was provided, yields items in order (reusing last or wrapping as needed per implementation); if LCG, computes a reproducible in-bounds Position.
  Constraints: standard library only; must be deterministic for tests.

- Module: snake_game.food
  - place_food(grid: Grid, rng: RandomProvider, occupied: set[Position]) -> Position: repeatedly obtains candidates via rng.next_position(grid) until an in-bounds candidate not in 'occupied' is found; returns that Position. Called only after consumption; no side effects beyond returning a Position.

- Module: snake_game.game
  - class Game:
    - __init__(self, grid: Grid, rng: RandomProvider, start: Position, direction: Direction): constructs a live game: initializes Snake, places initial food not on snake, sets score=0 and over=False; no second init call required.
    - turn(self, requested: Direction) -> bool: forwards to Snake.turn; returns whether the turn was accepted.
    - step(self) -> None: computes next_head once; determines grow = True iff next_head equals current food; checks hit_wall and hit_self before any mutation; if collision, sets over=True and returns; else advances snake with grow flag; if grow: increments score by 1; places new food via food.place_food only after consumption.
    - reset(self) -> None: resets game to initial start, initial direction, score=0, over=False, and places a new initial food not on snake using the same rng.
    - state(self) -> dict: returns a flat dict with keys: width:int, height:int, snake:list[tuple[int,int]], food:tuple[int,int], score:int, over:bool, direction:str. Direction is a stable string name ("UP","DOWN","LEFT","RIGHT"). Snake is ordered head-first list of (x,y) tuples; food is (x,y) tuple.
    - is_over(self) -> bool: returns current terminal flag.
    - score_get(self) -> int: returns current score.
  Import graph: game.py may import direction, grid, snake, collision, food, random_provider only; must maintain acyclic imports.

- Module: snake_game.__init__
  - Exposes from snake_game import Direction, Position, Grid, Snake, RandomProvider, Game as the canonical public API.

- Module: Main.py
  - main() -> None: constructs deterministic RandomProvider and Game, performs at most two safe steps, prints exactly one state snapshot (e.g., repr or formatted dict) and exits; only runs under if __name__ == "__main__": main().

- Module: tests/test_main.py
  - Deterministically imports canonical public API symbols explicitly (no wildcards): from snake_game import Direction, Position, Grid, Game, RandomProvider. Executes two concise tests (no-growth and growth fixtures) using python -m pytest -q.

General constraints:
- Python 3.10 only; avoid typing.Self, StrEnum, exception groups, or any 3.11+ APIs.
- Maintain acyclic import graph per protocol: direction -> none; grid -> none; snake -> direction+grid; collision -> grid; random_provider -> grid; food -> grid+random_provider; game -> direction, grid, snake, collision, food, random_provider.
- For any forward references within a module referencing its own types, start with: from __future__ import annotations; otherwise avoid forward references.
Shared Knowledge: Protocol requires preserving files exactly: requirements.txt lists pytest only; runtime entry is Main.py; single test file tests/test_main.py executed via python -m pytest -q. Tests import only those symbols explicitly and validate deterministic domain logic through Game.state without GUI, IO, or network.
Execution Protocol: Run: python -m pytest -q. Runtime entry: Main.py defines main(), runs only under __name__ guard, performs at most two safe steps, prints one snapshot, and exits.
